newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Norish says made good start to 1997.
newsitem.headline: Norish says made good start to 1997.

text.p: Irish industrial holding group Norish Plc said on Wednesday that the group made a positive start to the year and underlying profitability was ahead of 1996.
"The first quarter had lived up to expectations and there was a continuing strong undertone to the trade," executive chairman Brian Joyce told shareholders at an annual meeting.
Joyce said Norish has completed a major rationalisation and disposal programme in 1996 and was now concentrating most of its focus on the British commercial sector.

"The increased demand for space and the consequential rise in achievable prices for storage has meant that underlying profitability in the early part of 1997 was ahead of the comparable period in 1996," Joyce said.
He said restructuring and a return to profitability has meant that balance sheet debt will have to be reduced to "negligible levels" by the end of 1997 to leave scope for further development.
